post.title: Why You Scroll for an Hour and Watch Nothing #shorts
post.description: Scroller or picker? Tell me in the comments. Send this to the friend who scrolls more than they watch. Mae has endless choices on her streaming app, and watches nothing. In 2000, Sheena Iyengar and Mark Lepper (Journal of Personality and Social Psychology) set up a jam-tasting table in an upscale grocery store. With 24 jams on display, more passing shoppers stopped (about 60% vs 40%), but only about 3% of those who stopped bought a jar. With 6 jams, about 30% did. They called it choice overload: too many options can make deciding feel harder and less satisfying. Honest footnote: later meta-analyses found the effect isn't universal (Scheibehenne, Greifeneder & Todd, 2010); it shows up most when the options are hard to compare and you don't know what you want (Chernev, Böckenholt & Goodman, 2015). Try it: pick three, then choose. Comment 'got me' if you've scrolled past your own bedtime. #psychology #shorts #overthinking #choiceoverload #decisionmaking
